correctness.rationale: The defining identity is exactly the statement that A commutes with conjugation by every element in its image; closure under products and inverses upgrades this to equivariance under H=<A(G)>, and the converse is immediate. For S3, the four possible generated-image subgroup types are exhausted. Their conjugation-orbit decompositions give 1,45,80,3 maps and 1,21,26,3 pointed maps. Burnside counting under Aut(S3)=Inn(S3) gives 60 and 25 classes. The packaged checker exhaustively verifies all 6^6 maps and all automorphism orbits.

value.rationale: S3 is the smallest nonabelian group, so it is the first natural finite test case for the new conjugation-based averaging notion rather than an arbitrary finite slice. The subgroup-equivariance criterion gives a reusable method for finite-group enumeration and explains the census structurally. The exact counts show that the source's standard example families do not exhaust even the smallest nonabelian case, while the automorphism quotient separates genuine operator types from relabelings.
